preconditions.expression: all(c in 'abcdefghijklmnopqrst' for c in A) and all(c in 'abcdefghijklmnopqrst' for c in B)
preconditions.description: Both strings A and B consist only of the first 20 lowercase English letters ('a' to 't').

preconditions.expression: len(A) == len(B) and len(A) >= 1 and len(A) <= 10**5
preconditions.description: Strings A and B have the same length n, where 1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5.
The number of test cases t satisfies 1 ≤ t ≤ 10.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == '-1' if any(A[i] != B[i] and A[i] not in 'abcdefghijklmnopqrst' for i in range(len(A))) else stdout.strip()
postconditions.description: If there exists at least one position i where A[i] cannot be transformed to B[i] (i.e., B[i] is not in the first 20 letters or A[i] is not in the first 20 letters), output -1.

postconditions.expression: all(A[i] == B[i] for i in range(len(A))) if stdout.strip() == '0' else True
postconditions.description: If the output is 0, then A and B are already equal.

postconditions.expression: all(A[i] == B[i] for i in range(len(A))) or (int(stdout.strip()) >= 1 and int(stdout.strip()) <= len(A))
postconditions.description: If the output is a positive integer k, then it is possible to make A equal to B in exactly k moves, where each move transforms a subset of identical characters in A to any of the first 20 letters.

postconditions.expression: int(stdout.strip()) == min_moves if any(A[i] != B[i] for i in range(len(A))) else True
postconditions.description: The output is the smallest number of moves required to make A equal to B, where min_moves is the minimal k such that A can be transformed to B in k moves. If no such k exists, output -1.
